Duration-like property bags are read and converted in alphabetical order; ISO duration strings preserve fractional time units exactly. Mixed signs, nonintegral fields, calendar-field limits and the normalized 2^53-second bound are validated. Immutable result operations create base Duration values without consulting constructor or species overrides. add and subtract support day/time units, with exact integer nanosecond arithmetic, balancing to the largest input unit, correctly rounded binary64 fields and result-range validation; years, months and weeks are rejected. Numeric compare preserves nanosecond precision and short-circuits identical slots. total supports fixed units from day through nanosecond with one correctly rounded conversion of the exact ratio. Calendar-relative comparison and totals, supplied relativeTo values, time zones and Duration.round remain unsupported. toString and toJSON produce ISO duration strings; toString supports fractional-second precision, second-or-finer smallestUnit and nine signed rounding modes. toLocaleString uses the base ISO representation, not Intl.DurationFormat. valueOf rejects numeric coercion with TypeError. This development-branch coverage does not imply full Temporal support. |

Supports the ToBigInt constructor, exact epoch factories, branded epoch getters with floor-based milliseconds, ISO date-time parsing with explicit offsets, extended Gregorian years, leap seconds and annotation validation, from, compare and equals. Instant-like objects must convert to string primitives. add/subtract accept time units and reject nonzero day/calendar fields; results preserve exact BigInt arithmetic and the Instant range. since/until create intrinsic Duration values, preserving conversion and option access order, increment validation, signed rounding, exact balancing, positive-zero fields and binary64 slot conversion. Unit names are validated on read; unit-group validation follows the remaining option reads. round supports six time units and nine timeline-directed modes, including pre-epoch instants and whole-day-dividing increments. toJSON and toString provide UTC ISO formatting; toString also supports UTC and minute-precision fixed-offset time zones, including ISO date/time strings identifying those zones and offset date rollover at the Instant boundaries. Time-zone values must be strings, not coercible objects. toLocaleString uses the base ISO representation without Intl.DateTimeFormat.
